title: Audio and Speech Generative AI
summary: This day covers essential concepts for building AI engineering skills.
content:
# Audio and Speech Generative AI ##### 4.2 seconds of silence A team in Hyderabad built a voice assistant for field agents — technicians who needed hands-free access to equipment manuals while working. Technically it worked: Whisper transcribed, GPT-4 answered from a RAG index, and a TTS API spoke the response. Median latency from the user finishing speaking to hearing the first word of the reply: **4.2 seconds.** In text that would be tolerable. In conversation it was unusable. Field agents repeated themselves, thinking the system had not heard, which triggered a second transcription and made it worse. The breakdown was revealing: | Stage | Latency | Fixable? | |---|---|---| | Waiting for speech to end (silence detection) | 900ms | Yes — tune VAD | | Whisper transcription (full audio) | 1,100ms | Yes — stream it | | LLM generation (full response) | 1,600ms | Yes — stream to TTS | | TTS synthesis (full text) | 600ms | Yes — chunk it | Every stage waited for the previous one to *complete*. Nothing was streamed. Restructured as a streaming pipeline, first-audio latency dropped to **780ms** — conversational. The model was identical; only the plumbing changed. **Voice pipelines are a latency engineering problem far more than a model quality problem.** Day 39 of the beginner track introduced Whisper; today is the full pipeline and the latency budget that makes it usable. ##### The voice pipeline ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Microphone"] --> B["VAD
detect speech"] B --> C["Streaming ASR
partial transcripts"] C --> D{"Endpoint
detected?"} D -->|no| C D -->|yes| E["LLM
streaming tokens"] E --> F["Sentence chunker"] F --> G["Streaming TTS"] G --> H["Audio playback"] E -.->|"first sentence"| F F -.->|"synthesise while
LLM still generating"| G I["Barge-in: user speaks
→ cancel everything"] -.-> B ``` **The critical design principle: every stage starts before the previous one finishes.** ASR emits partial transcripts, the LLM starts on the first stable transcript, TTS synthesises the first sentence while the LLM is still writing the third. ##### ASR with Whisper Day 39 covered the basics. Here is what production needs. ```python from faster_whisper import WhisperModel import numpy as np model = WhisperModel( "large-v3", device="cuda", compute_type="float16", # int8_float16 on smaller GPUs num_workers=2, ) segments, info = model.transcribe( "field_recording.wav", language="hi", # None to auto-detect (costs ~200ms) task="transcribe", beam_size=5, vad_filter=True, # skip silence — large speedup vad_parameters={"min_silence_duration_ms": 500, "speech_pad_ms": 200}, condition_on_previous_text=False, # ← prevents hallucination loops initial_prompt="Technical vocabulary: compressor, solenoid, PSI, RPM.", word_timestamps=True, ) for seg in segments: print(f"[{seg.start:.2f}-{seg.end:.2f}] {seg.text}") ``` **`condition_on_previous_text=False` prevents a specific and nasty failure.** With it enabled, Whisper conditions each segment on the previous transcription, and on silence or noise it can enter a loop repeating the same phrase indefinitely. Anyone who has seen a transcript containing "thank you for watching" forty times has met this bug. **`initial_prompt` is an underused lever.** Seeding domain vocabulary measurably improves recognition of technical terms, product names, and Indian proper nouns that Whisper otherwise mangles. **faster-whisper over openai-whisper.** The CTranslate2 implementation is roughly 4× faster at equal accuracy and uses substantially less memory — there is no reason to use the reference implementation in production. **For Indian languages**, model size matters more than for English: | Model | English WER | Hindi WER | Tamil WER | Speed | |---|---|---|---|---| | tiny | 12.1% | 38.4% | 51.2% | 32× | | base | 9.8% | 31.7% | 44.6% | 16× | | small | 7.2% | 22.3% | 33.1% | 6× | | medium | 5.9% | 16.8% | 25.4% | 2× | | **large-v3** | **4.8%** | **11.2%** | **17.9%** | 1× | | **IndicWhisper** | 6.1% | **8.4%** | **11.3%** | 2× | **AI4Bharat's IndicWhisper is substantially better on Indian languages** and worth evaluating for any Indic deployment. Code-mixed Hinglish — extremely common in real Indian speech — is where the gap is largest. ##### Voice activity detection and endpointing The first 900ms of the Hyderabad latency, and the easiest to fix. ```python import torch import numpy as np from collections import deque class StreamingVAD: """Silero VAD with adaptive endpointing.""" def __init__(self, sample_rate=16000, threshold=0.5, min_speech_ms=250, min_silence_ms=600, max_utterance_s=30): self.model, _ = torch.hub.load("snakers4/silero-vad", "silero_vad", trust_repo=True) self.sr = sample_rate self.threshold = threshold self.frame_samples = 512 # 32ms at 16kHz self.min_speech_frames = min_speech_ms // 32 self.min_silence_frames = min_silence_ms // 32 self.max_frames = int(max_utterance_s * 1000 / 32) self.buffer = [] self.speech_frames = 0 self.silence_frames = 0 self.in_speech = False def process(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> dict: """Feed 32ms frames. Returns state transitions.""" tensor = torch.from_numpy(frame).float() prob = float(self.model(tensor, self.sr).item()) is_speech = prob > self.threshold if is_speech: self.speech_frames += 1 self.silence_frames = 0 self.buffer.append(frame) if not self.in_speech and self.speech_frames >= self.min_speech_frames: self.in_speech = True return {"event": "speech_start", "prob": prob} else: if self.in_speech: self.silence_frames += 1 self.buffer.append(frame) # keep trailing silence if self.silence_frames >= self.min_silence_frames: audio = np.concatenate(self.buffer) self._reset() return {"event": "speech_end", "audio": audio, "duration_s": len(audio) / self.sr} else: self.speech_frames = 0 if len(self.buffer) >= self.max_frames: audio = np.concatenate(self.buffer) self._reset() return {"event": "max_duration", "audio": audio} return {"event": "continue", "prob": prob} def _reset(self): self.buffer, self.speech_frames = [], 0 self.silence_frames, self.in_speech = 0, False ``` **`min_silence_ms` is the direct latency-versus-interruption trade.** At 300ms the system feels instant but cuts people off mid-thought; at 1,000ms it never interrupts but feels sluggish. **600ms is the usual compromise**, and it can be adapted — shorter after a question, longer mid-explanation. **Semantic endpointing** is the more sophisticated approach: use the partial transcript to decide whether the utterance is grammatically complete. "What is the pressure rating for the—" is clearly unfinished regardless of the pause length. ##### Streaming ASR Do not wait for the utterance to end before transcribing. ```python import asyncio import numpy as np from faster_whisper import WhisperModel class StreamingTranscriber: """Transcribe a growing buffer, emitting stable partial results.""" def __init__(self, model: WhisperModel, sample_rate=16000, chunk_seconds=1.0, stability_threshold=2): self.model = model self.sr = sample_rate self.chunk_samples = int(chunk_seconds * sample_rate) self.audio = np.array([], dtype=np.float32) self.stable_text = "" self.pending_history = [] self.stability_threshold = stability_threshold async def add_audio(self, chunk: np.ndarray) -> dict: self.audio = np.concatenate([self.audio, chunk]) if len(self.audio) < self.chunk_samples: return {"partial": self.stable_text, "stable": self.stable_text} segments, _ = await asyncio.to_thread( self.model.transcribe, self.audio, language="hi", beam_size=1, # beam 1 for speed condition_on_previous_text=False, vad_filter=False, # VAD already applied upstream ) text = " ".join(s.text for s in segments).strip() # A prefix is "stable" once it repeats across N consecutive passes self.pending_history.append(text) if len(self.pending_history) > self.stability_threshold: self.pending_history.pop(0) if len(self.pending_history) == self.stability_threshold: stable = self._common_prefix(self.pending_history) if len(stable) > len(self.stable_text): self.stable_text = stable return {"partial": text, "stable": self.stable_text, "newly_stable": self.stable_text != text} @staticmethod def _common_prefix(texts: list[str]) -> str: if not texts: return "" words = [t.split() for t in texts] prefix = [] for group in zip(*words): if len(set(group)) == 1: prefix.append(group[0]) else: break return " ".join(prefix) ``` **The stability heuristic matters** because Whisper revises its output as more audio arrives — "the pressure" can become "the pressure rating" and then "depression rating" before settling. Emitting unstable text to the LLM produces confused responses; waiting for a prefix to repeat across two passes gives you text safe to act on. **Purpose-built streaming ASR** — Deepgram, AssemblyAI, or NVIDIA Riva — handles this natively and is worth considering. Whisper was designed for batch transcription, and streaming it is a workaround. ##### Text-to-speech The final stage, and the one where perceived quality lives. ```python from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Literal, AsyncIterator @dataclass class TTSConfig: provider: Literal["elevenlabs", "openai", "azure", "coqui", "piper"] voice_id: str speed: float = 1.0 streaming: bool = True sample_rate: int = 24000 format: str = "pcm" # PCM avoids decode latency TTS_OPTIONS = { "elevenlabs": {"quality": "excellent", "latency_ms": 300, "streaming": True, "cost": "high", "indic": "limited", "cloning": "excellent"}, "openai_tts": {"quality": "very good", "latency_ms": 400, "streaming": True, "cost": "moderate", "indic": "moderate", "cloning": "no"}, "azure_neural": {"quality": "very good", "latency_ms": 350, "streaming": True, "cost": "moderate", "indic": "excellent — 12 Indian languages", "cloning": "yes"}, "coqui_xtts": {"quality": "good", "latency_ms": 600, "streaming": True, "cost": "self-hosted", "indic": "moderate", "cloning": "yes, 6s sample"}, "piper": {"quality": "moderate", "latency_ms": 80, "streaming": True, "cost": "self-hosted, CPU", "indic": "some", "cloning": "no"}, } ``` **Azure Neural TTS is generally the strongest option for Indian languages**, with genuinely good Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, and Bengali voices. Piper is remarkable for edge deployment — it runs on a Raspberry Pi at 80ms latency. **Streaming TTS with sentence chunking** is the third latency fix: ```python import re import asyncio from typing import AsyncIterator SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?।])\s+") CLAUSE_BREAK = re.compile(r"(?<=[,;:])\s+") async def chunk_for_tts(token_stream: AsyncIterator[str], min_chars=40, max_chars=200) -> AsyncIterator[str]: """Emit speakable chunks as the LLM generates, not after it finishes.""" buffer = "" async for token in token_stream: buffer += token # Prefer sentence boundaries parts = SENTENCE_END.split(buffer) if len(parts) > 1: for complete in parts[:-1]: if complete.strip(): yield complete.strip() buffer = parts[-1] continue # Fall back to clause breaks if the sentence is running long if len(buffer) >= max_chars: clauses = CLAUSE_BREAK.split(buffer) if len(clauses) > 1: yield " ".join(clauses[:-1]).strip() buffer = clauses[-1] if buffer.strip(): yield buffer.strip() ``` **The Devanagari danda `।`** in the sentence regex again — the same detail as Day 4 and Day 20. Without it, an entire Hindi response is one chunk and you lose all streaming benefit. **Chunking at clause boundaries when sentences run long** prevents a 300-character sentence from stalling playback. The prosody is slightly worse than a full sentence, and it is far better than four seconds of silence. ##### The complete streaming pipeline ```python import asyncio import time from dataclasses import dataclass, field @dataclass class VoiceTurnMetrics: speech_end_ts: float = 0.0 transcript_ready_ts: float = 0.0 first_token_ts: float = 0.0 first_audio_ts: float = 0.0 complete_ts: float = 0.0 def summary(self) -> dict: base = self.speech_end_ts return { "asr_ms": round((self.transcript_ready_ts - base) * 1000, 1), "llm_ttft_ms": round((self.first_token_ts - self.transcript_ready_ts) * 1000, 1), "tts_first_audio_ms": round((self.first_audio_ts - self.first_token_ts) * 1000, 1), "total_to_first_audio_ms": round((self.first_audio_ts - base) * 1000, 1), "total_turn_ms": round((self.complete_ts - base) * 1000, 1), } class VoiceAgent: def __init__(self, transcriber, llm_client, tts_client, vad, rag_retriever=None): self.transcriber = transcriber self.llm = llm_client self.tts = tts_client self.vad = vad self.retriever = rag_retriever self.history = [] self._cancel = asyncio.Event() async def handle_turn(self, audio_stream, audio_output) -> VoiceTurnMetrics: metrics = VoiceTurnMetrics() self._cancel.clear() # 1. VAD + streaming ASR concurrently transcript = await self._listen(audio_stream, metrics) if not transcript.strip(): return metrics # 2. Retrieval (if RAG) — overlaps with nothing, so keep it fast context = "" if self.retriever: chunks = await self.retriever(transcript, k=3) context = "\n\n".join(c["text"] for c in chunks) # 3. LLM streaming → TTS streaming, pipelined self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": transcript}) token_stream = self.llm.stream( messages=self._build_messages(context), max_tokens=250, # keep spoken answers short ) first_token = True full_response = "" async for chunk in chunk_for_tts(token_stream): if self._cancel.is_set(): break if first_token: metrics.first_token_ts = time.perf_counter() first_token = False async for audio_bytes in self.tts.stream(chunk): if self._cancel.is_set(): break if metrics.first_audio_ts == 0.0: metrics.first_audio_ts = time.perf_counter() await audio_output.write(audio_bytes) full_response += chunk + " " self.history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": full_response.strip()}) metrics.complete_ts = time.perf_counter() return metrics async def barge_in(self): """User started speaking — cancel generation and playback.""" self._cancel.set() def _build_messages(self, context: str) -> list[dict]: system = ( "You are a voice assistant for field technicians. " "CRITICAL: Your response will be spoken aloud. " "Keep answers under 3 sentences. Use plain words. " "Never use markdown, bullet points, or symbols. " "Spell out numbers and units: say 'forty five PSI' not '45 PSI'. " "If you do not know, say so briefly." ) if context: system += f"\n\nRelevant manual excerpts:\n{context}" return [{"role": "system", "content": system}, *self.history[-8:]] ``` **The system prompt doing voice-specific work is essential.** A response written for reading — with markdown, bullet points, and "45 PSI" — sounds terrible spoken. Instructing brevity and plain formatting is the highest-return prompt change in a voice pipeline. **Barge-in matters more than it seems.** A user must be able to interrupt, and the system must stop speaking immediately. Without it, users talk over the assistant, the ASR picks up the TTS output, and the conversation collapses. ##### The latency budget The assignment. Work backwards from what feels conversational. ```python @dataclass class LatencyBudget: """Human conversation tolerates ~500-800ms gaps. Above 1.5s feels broken.""" target_first_audio_ms: float = 800 vad_endpoint_ms: float = 600 # tunable, biggest single chunk asr_ms: float = 150 # streaming makes this small retrieval_ms: float = 80 llm_ttft_ms: float = 350 tts_first_chunk_ms: float = 300 network_overhead_ms: float = 100 @property def naive_total(self) -> float: """Sequential — every stage waits for the last.""" return (self.vad_endpoint_ms + self.asr_ms + self.retrieval_ms + self.llm_ttft_ms + self.tts_first_chunk_ms + self.network_overhead_ms) @property def streamed_total(self) -> float: """ASR overlaps with speech; TTS overlaps with generation.""" return (self.vad_endpoint_ms + self.retrieval_ms + self.llm_ttft_ms + self.tts_first_chunk_ms * 0.4 + self.network_overhead_ms) b = LatencyBudget() print(f"naive: {b.naive_total:.0f}ms, streamed: {b.streamed_total:.0f}ms") # naive: 1580ms, streamed: 1250ms ``` **Optimisation priorities, in order of return:** | Optimisation | Saving | Difficulty | |---|---|---| | **Stream TTS from LLM tokens** | 400–1,200ms | Moderate | | **Reduce `min_silence_ms` to 500** | 100–400ms | Trivial | | **Stream ASR during speech** | 300–900ms | Moderate | | Smaller/faster LLM for voice | 200–600ms | Easy | | Prefix-cache the system prompt | 100–300ms | Trivial (Day 32) | | Co-locate services in one region | 50–200ms | Easy | | Semantic endpointing | 100–300ms | Hard | | Self-host TTS (Piper) | 200–400ms | Moderate | **Use a smaller model for voice than for text.** Spoken answers are short — under 250 tokens — and the quality difference between an 8B and a 70B model on a three-sentence answer is much smaller than the latency difference. **Measure the actual distribution, not the mean:** ```python import numpy as np def analyse_voice_latency(turn_metrics: list[VoiceTurnMetrics]) -> dict: summaries = [m.summary() for m in turn_metrics] out = {} for key in summaries[0]: values = [s[key] for s in summaries] out[key] = { "p50": round(float(np.percentile(values, 50)), 1), "p95": round(float(np.percentile(values, 95)), 1), "max": round(float(np.max(values)), 1), } total = [s["total_to_first_audio_ms"] for s in summaries] out["pct_under_1s"] = round(float(np.mean(np.array(total) < 1000)) * 100, 1) return out ``` **Report the fraction of turns under one second.** That single number predicts whether users find the system conversational better than any percentile. ##### Voice cloning and ethics ```python from TTS.api import TTS tts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to("cuda") tts.tts_to_file( text="कृपया कंप्रेसर का दबाव जांचें।", speaker_wav="reference_voice.wav", # 6+ seconds of clean speech language="hi", file_path="output.wav", ) ``` **XTTS-v2 clones a voice from about six seconds of audio** across 17 languages. The quality is good enough to be genuinely useful and good enough to be genuinely dangerous. **The obligations are not optional:** - **Explicit consent** from the voice owner, documented and specific to the use. - **Disclosure** that the voice is synthetic, in any context where a listener might assume otherwise. - **Watermarking** where available — AudioSeal and similar embed detectable signals. - **No impersonation** of real people without documented consent. - **Retention limits** on voice samples, which are biometric data under the DPDP Act 2023 and require heightened protection. India's IT Rules amendments and the EU AI Act both push toward mandatory disclosure of synthetic media. Beyond compliance, voice cloning fraud targeting Indian families — the "distressed relative" scam using a cloned voice — is a real and growing harm, and building in this space carries responsibility. ##### Audio tokenization Worth understanding because it is where the field is heading. **Neural audio codecs** — EnCodec, SoundStream, DAC — compress audio into discrete tokens, which lets a language model generate audio the same way it generates text. ```python from transformers import EncodecModel, AutoProcessor import torch model = EncodecModel.from_pretrained("facebook/encodec_24khz") processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("facebook/encodec_24khz") inputs = processor(raw_audio=audio_array, sampling_rate=24000, return_tensors="pt") with torch.no_grad(): encoded = model.encode(inputs["input_values"], inputs["padding_mask"]) codes = encoded.audio_codes # (batch, n_codebooks, n_frames) — discrete print(f"{len(audio_array)/24000:.1f}s → {codes.shape[-1]} frames × " f"{codes.shape[1]} codebooks") decoded = model.decode(encoded.audio_codes, encoded.audio_scales, inputs["padding_mask"])[0] ``` **This is what enables end-to-end speech models.** GPT-4o's voice mode and Moshi do not run a three-stage pipeline — they process audio tokens directly, which eliminates the ASR and TTS stages entirely and brings latency toward 300ms while preserving prosody, emotion, and interruption handling that a text bottleneck destroys. **The three-stage pipeline is the current practical approach and a transitional one.** Build it now; expect end-to-end models to replace it. ##### Common mistakes - **Sequential stages** with no streaming — the 4.2-second gap. - **`condition_on_previous_text=True`**, causing Whisper hallucination loops. - **`min_silence_ms` too high**, adding a second of dead air to every turn. - **No barge-in**, so users cannot interrupt. - **TTS picking up its own output** without echo cancellation or muting during playback. - **Markdown and symbols in responses** destined to be spoken. - **Long responses** — a 400-word answer takes two minutes to speak. - **English-only sentence splitting** on Hindi text, defeating chunking. - **Whisper `tiny` or `base` for Indian languages**, where WER exceeds 30%. - **No domain `initial_prompt`**, mangling technical vocabulary. - **Voice cloning without documented consent** or disclosure. - **Reporting mean latency** instead of the fraction of turns under one second. ##### Hands-on: build it, then stream it Your practical task builds an ASR-to-LLM-to-TTS pipeline. **Build the naive sequential version first and measure it** — you need that baseline to know what streaming buys, and the number will be worse than you expect. Then instrument each stage with the `VoiceTurnMetrics` structure so you know exactly where the time goes before optimising. The mini project creates a real-time voice assistant with streaming at every stage. Implement barge-in early rather than as an afterthought; retrofitting cancellation through a pipeline is harder than designing for it. Test with Hindi or a code-mixed input if your users will speak that way — the sentence-splitting and model-size issues only appear with real language. The assignment analyses latency sources and proposes optimisations. Use the budget breakdown, report p50 and p95 and the fraction of turns under one second, and rank your proposed optimisations by milliseconds saved per unit of effort. A recommendation that says "streaming TTS saves 800ms for two days of work; semantic endpointing saves 200ms for two weeks" is the analysis that gets acted on. ##### Key takeaways - **Voice is a latency problem.** Every stage must start before the previous one finishes, and streaming TTS from LLM tokens is the single largest win. - **Tune `min_silence_ms` deliberately** — it is a direct trade between responsiveness and cutting people off, and 600ms is the usual compromise. - **Set `condition_on_previous_text=False`** and seed domain vocabulary with `initial_prompt`; use `large-v3` or IndicWhisper for Indian languages. - **Write the system prompt for speech**: under three sentences, no markdown, spelled-out numbers — this is the cheapest quality improvement available. - **Voice cloning requires documented consent, disclosure, and watermarking** — voice samples are biometric data, and cloning fraud is a real harm, not a hypothetical one.
practical_task_reference: Build an ASR-to-LLM-to-TTS pipeline that transcribes speech, answers with an LLM, and speaks the response.
mini_project_reference: Create a real-time voice assistant with streaming transcription, LLM reasoning, and low-latency TTS.
assignment_reference: Analyze latency sources in a voice pipeline and propose optimizations to reach conversational latency.
